pairs.difference: A: the jacket has quiet soft cloth folds, thin pocket seams and small embossed sash badges, though no visible weave. B: the hat crown and brim are one seamless clay-smooth skin. There is no felt nap, crease or edge stitching, and the band and star are as soft as the hat. Weak call: real cards also smooth materials, and gloss numbers do not separate the two.
pairs.fix: Give the hat dry brushed felt with a very fine nap, tiny scuffs along the brim edge, a thin stitched line around the brim, and a star concho in matte metal with a small crisp highlight.

pairs.difference: A: this is a frontal redraw of the real ship-wheel subject. Thin grain lines run evenly around the ring and base, the deck carries drawn cracks and scratch lines, and the hub is mirror gold against satin wood. B: soft painted plastic bottles with quiet water specks and a matte label, slightly blurred up close but with no added surface marks. A's texture feels applied as decoration.
pairs.fix: Keep the wood smooth and satin, with only a few faint broad grain tones. Remove the cracks and scratch lines from the deck planks.

pairs.difference: A: the red cloth is smooth and satin with soft folds, and the badge is simple and embossed. This matches the real cards' habit of smoothing material. B: every rope strand carries dense fine fibre streaks at the same scale and direction along the whole coil. That is the over-fine added detail the later lesson generations showed, and the micro-texture sits near the top of the real range.
pairs.fix: Paint the rope as smooth rounded twisted strands with soft shading, and drop the hair-like fibre lines. Keep only a few faint marks where strands turn.

pairs.difference: A: the boat planks are simplified with faint grain, soft satin rails and rope with plain twist. B: the wagon adds small brass rivets on each red strap, fine canvas puckers and seams, and a separate grain treatment on each board. The finish is credible, but it has more small hardware than the real cards carry. Numbers are nearly equal, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Remove most of the small rivets, simplify the canvas to a few broad soft folds, and let the wood boards be smooth with only faint tonal grain.

pairs.difference: B: this computer matches the real lesson card, with smooth matte beige plastic and a soft screen sheen. A: the saddle leather has double stitch-like edge grooves, punched strap holes, a shiny bevel on every panel and bright rivets. The fence behind it has nearly photographic weathered grain and knots, far finer and more literal than the toy-smooth real surfaces.
pairs.fix: Simplify the leather to smooth soft-sheen panels with one or two thin seams, drop the punched holes, and paint the fence as plain soft planks with almost no grain or knots.

pairs.difference: A: the chest wood has quiet low-contrast plank lines, and the coins and gold trim have simple clean sheens with small dents. B: the barrel staves carry big looping cathedral grain as a decorative pattern, the iron bands have drawn hairline scratches, and a smeared orange blotch sits on one stave. The grain scale is too large and the wear looks applied.
pairs.fix: Use faint straight fine grain on the staves, remove the orange stain, and make the iron bands clean dull metal with a soft highlight and no scratches.

pairs.difference: A: the doors are one lacquered orange finish on frame and louvres, with hazy soft edges and blotchy pale panel grain, so wood reads as coated plastic. B: the shoes separate materials, with a fine dotted mesh upper, a matte foam sole and rubbery laces, though the mesh is dense and busy. B's gloss and micro-texture sit at the real ceiling. Low confidence, because B also looks odd.
pairs.fix: Make the door frames a dry satin wood with subtle grain and slightly darker worn edges, and keep gloss low on the louvres so they do not read as orange plastic.

pairs.difference: A: the mug body is covered in long horizontal brushed-metal streaks that look like visible smeared strokes, with the same sheen on rim and handle, and low overall detail. The tabletop has decorative grain and a knot. B: the roses and leaves have clean small forms and quiet soft petals. Its high numbers come from the dense foliage rather than from a surface fault.
pairs.fix: Paint the mug as smooth pale tin with soft broad reflections, a crisp small highlight on the rim, and no streaky brushed lines.

pairs.difference: A: the boot leather has a uniform lacquered sheen on the shaft and toe, with thin stitch lines tracing each overlay and pipe, and the leather has no matte zone. B: the cap is plain soft matte board with a crisp edge and restrained detail, closer to the real cards' quiet smoothing. Weak call, since the cap also shows no cloth weave.
pairs.fix: Lower the shine on the boot shaft, keep a soft highlight only on the toe, and reduce the stitching to one or two thin seams.

pairs.difference: A: the book cover is a smooth flat satin with crisp sticker edges, but the desk behind has large decorative grain bands. B: the sign boxes are thick glossy orange enamel throughout, with glassy tube highlights and a soft bloom. The whole object is one lacquer, and gloss is well above the real range (0.18 against 0.119). Weak call given A's chunky desk grain.
pairs.fix: Give the sign frames dull painted metal with a soft sheen, keep the shine only on the neon tubes, and make the posts plain matte.

pairs.difference: A: the coaster cars are smooth candy-gloss plastic with broad clean highlights, matching the simple real cards. B: the locomotive has many small rivets, pipes and a fine brass bell, and its black boiler is an even satin that makes everything look like one moulded material. Gloss is just above the real range (0.227 against 0.209).
pairs.fix: Reduce the small rivets and fittings, add a brighter sheen band along the boiler, and make the bell clearly polished brass against duller iron.

pairs.difference: A: the cactus is one inflated glossy rubber skin, and its spines are enlarged yellow pills, a chunky toy detail. There is no waxy matte variation along the ribs. B: the popcorn cart mixes materials well, with a matte red body, clear glass with a streak reflection, soft kernels and a paper tub. Gloss is above the real ceiling by a hair on A.
pairs.fix: Make the cactus skin waxy and mostly matte with faint vertical tone along the ribs, and replace the yellow pills with thin small pale spines.

pattern: Generated cards are given away by added surface decoration and by a single finish across the object. Fine marks are laid evenly everywhere: fibre streaks on rope, brushed lines on metal, scratches on iron bands, stitch lines on every leather edge. Grain is oversized or looping, and rivets and small hardware multiply. Each material still carries the same lacquer or clay skin, so gloss does not vary within the object. Real cards stay quieter: broad smooth forms, a few restrained seams, and shine kept to one or two places. Most calls here are low confidence, because the real cards also smooth materials and these pairs show different subjects.
